method: Expectations come from dispatch.c and, for the symbols and for which calls are jumps, from the system tools nm and otool -tV run on the two built files, not from any engine under test. Verified in the built files: both have the undefined symbols atoi, getenv, printf, puts, remove, strcmp, strlen and no other; both have a symbol for main and for each of the nine static functions (every one is noinline, none was inlined or dropped). At -O0 every call in the source is a bl (main has bl usage twice, tree_sum has bl tree_sum twice) and the call through the table is blr. At -O2 these are jumps (b): main -> usage (one jump for both source calls), main -> finish, usage -> emit, cmd_env -> emit, emit -> puts; these stay bl: main -> lookup, lookup -> plausible, lookup -> strcmp (twice, the loop is unrolled), plausible -> strlen, finish -> tree_sum, finish -> printf, cmd_double -> atoi, cmd_env -> getenv, audit_cleanup -> remove, tree_sum -> tree_sum (once; the second recursive call became a loop); the call through the table is still blr in main. So printf is reachable from main only through the jump main -> finish, and puts from main only through three jumps in a row. A path means a chain of direct calls or jumps to named functions; the call through the pointer table is not part of any expected path, and no question is asked whose answer depends on it. Callers are the functions that contain a direct call or jump to the function.

paths.why: main calls lookup, lookup calls plausible, plausible calls strlen; ordinary calls at both levels
lookup calls strcmp in its loop; ordinary calls at both levels
main returns finish(), finish calls printf; at -O2 main -> finish is a jump and there is no other way from main to printf
main returns usage(), usage returns emit(), emit returns puts(); at -O2 all three are jumps and no call instruction lies on the way
finish calls tree_sum with an ordinary call; main reaches finish by a call (-O0) or a jump (-O2)
cmd_env returns emit(), emit returns puts(); two jumps at -O2
a direct call at both levels
remove is used only by audit_cleanup, which nothing calls and which is in no table
kept by the used attribute; no call, jump or table entry refers to it
lookup reaches plausible, strlen and strcmp only
finish reaches tree_sum and printf only
usage reaches emit and puts only; getenv is called by cmd_env, which calls emit, not the other way round
tree_sum calls only itself; printf is called by its caller finish, and a path does not run from a function back to its caller

callers.why: kept by the used attribute, called by nobody
reached only through the commands table (blr in main); no direct call exists, and a tool that reports no caller should not conclude it is dead
reached only through the commands table, like cmd_double
two calls at -O0, one jump at -O2
finish calls it and it calls itself; at -O2 one recursive call instruction remains
